text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan looks into ways to object eight year compulsory education as is pressurised by his grassroot. Erbakan earlier signed National Security Council (MGK) decisions of 18 steps to crack down on rising Islamist activism which includes the expanding of compulsory education to eight years Islamist activicism.

- Conservative coalition partner True Path Party (DYP) insists on the implementation of eight compulsory education whereas its Islamist coalition partner is allegedly gearing up to hand it back to MGK requesting review and change.
- Istanbul stroken haphazardly by snow March. Snow effeted the city trafficc.
- Riots in Buca Prison in coastal Izmir and in a prison northwestern Bursa by political prisoners.

- Head of the Central Bank Gazi Ercel says Islamist-led government has withdrawn the amount money that laws gives assess to a government. Government withdrew 283 billions Turkish lira from Central Bank in advance.
- Chairman of trade union DISK says ruling Islamist Welfare follows a polarisation policy in the public, mounts tension in society and is makes a call for a coup.
- Ercel says Turkey's signing a stand-by accord with International Monetary Fund (IMF) is not on the agenda.
- Students of religious high-schools denies having to do with politics.
